title: Quarterly tax planning meetings with your CPA
summary: Not just at tax time. Real-time tax planning is the difference between owing $50K and owing $150K on the same business profit.
detailsHtml:
What gets decided in these meetings

Estimated tax payments. Retirement plan contributions and their timing. Equipment purchases and Section 179 / bonus depreciation. Salary vs. distribution mix for S-corp owners. Reasonable salary documentation. QBI deduction optimization. State tax planning (PTET elections, multi-state apportionment). Year-end tax moves before December 31.

What it costs

A small-business CPA who does meaningful planning typically charges $3,000–$15,000/year depending on complexity. For most businesses generating $300K+ in profit, the tax savings vastly exceed the fees. The CPA who only files your return at year-end is providing a different (and lower-value) service.
